items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: The name Jug Burger springs to mind.

ctx.x: Well, let's... Let's go back a few years. Uh... It's possible that, uh... Uh... Fountain was influenced by, uh... A player that he admired very much, and we did get to know, uh... Fazzola. Uh... Do you think there's such a thing as a Fazzola influence in Chicago today?

Yeah. The name Jug Burger springs to mind. Uh-huh. Uh... Jug was very fond of... What was his nickname? Foz? Yes. And, uh... And Jug, I believe, is from New Orleans, or from Biloxi, or that neck of the woods. And he was very... Very fond of Foz. And his playing does reflect Foz's playing. But... I don't know if anybody can really do what Fozola did. I don't think Fountain does it. Although I think the influence is detectable there.
Well, Fountain speaks with great respect to Foz. And they were together enough that I think that it would be inevitable that he would understand Fozola very well.
